findings.title: New claims verified at 7404845f
findings.detail: (1) panel.json round is bumped in place. internal/panel/create.go: Create writes panel.json as a full-struct overwrite and never reads the existing file; panel.go:46-48 documents that Round and ReviewedHeadSHA co-bump in the same write; ms-panel-run SKILL.md:67 says the same. A single registration dir therefore holds only its latest round's SHA, and multiple rounds are visible to F2 only as separate dirs (the documented '-r2' slug convention, SKILL.md:28). AC-11's 'separate registration dirs, each with an explicit round' matches. (2) extractBeadSectionRaw is positional (readiness.go:281-310): it counts '## Bead ' headings and captures the Nth, ignoring the written number, exactly as R1.1(c) and AC-1's 1–7,12 fixture state. (3) TestReattest_HappyPathFleetState exists (reattest_test.go:93), with a re-run leg asserting Wrote=false and no extra writes. (4) bead.MergeMetadata (bdcli.go:322-349) is read-merge-write (GetMetadata, overlay updates, one bd update --metadata), and both the executor binding writer (mindspec_executor.go:1616 mergeBindingFn) and reattest (reattest.go:93 reattestBindingFn) use it. So an executor rewrite leaves prior mindspec_landed_reattest_* keys in place, as the stale-audit argument assumes. (5) reattestOp is the constant "mindspec reattest" (reattest.go:112), 'at' is written as RFC-3339 (:360), and the scanned_branch key exists, so the VALID-audit shape check has real anchors. (6) gitutil already has a 'git show <ref>:<path>' read (gitops.go:734), and internal/next already imports gitutil (guard.go). The lazy spec-branch plan.md read is therefore not a new boundary crossing.

findings.title: The #233 second parent is described as a 'tree-identical' commit; that matches the issue's older binary, not necessarily e2325e36
findings.detail: GH #233 observed a tree-identical wrapper commit ('impl(<id>): <summary>' with no diff from its parent) on the binary it was filed against. At e2325e36, mindspec complete runs spec 128 Bead 6's M/S staged protocol (internal/complete/materialize.go). The S(ync) stage commits the .beads/issues.jsonl export (stageArtifactSync), so the second parent can be one or more commits after the reviewed head that are NOT tree-identical. The executor's msg auto-commit (mindspec_executor.go:369) is a further possible commit. F2's anchor rule is 'reviewed_head_sha equals or is an ancestor of the second parent', so it is correct either way and does not depend on tree identity. Only the rationale text (R4.2 F2 'Anchors', AC-12(iv)) overstates it. Reword it to 'complete adds one or more commits after review (#233 saw a tree-identical wrapper; the current M/S stages may add a materialization commit and a JSONL-sync commit)', and keep OQ-3's plan-stage measurement as the place this is pinned.

findings.title: Attack on the anchor/round rule: no masquerade found; the round-default tie is fail-closed but worth naming
findings.detail: Can a later unlanded round masquerade as an anchor? An anchor needs reviewed_head_sha equal to or an ancestor of the candidate's second parent. A later round's SHA C is an ancestor of the second parent only if the landed history contains C, in which case C landed and is legitimately an anchor. Without forging panel.json (agent-writable, inside ADR-0037 §8's stated boundary), C cannot pass as an ancestor of the second parent while being unlanded. One operational edge: ms-panel-run's 'round' input defaults to 1 (SKILL.md:30), so an orchestrator that uses the '-r2' separate-slug convention but omits --round produces two dirs both at round 1. If one of them is a non-ancestor of the tip, F2 sees a tie and fails closed. That is safe, and the exits are named (scoped override, attested restore). But it is a plausible honest-operator refusal, and the F2 refusal text could say 'registrations <dirs> share round <n>' so the fix (re-register with explicit rounds) is obvious. Optional.
